name: Weak TLS minimum version pinned in code (tls.Config MinVersion/MaxVersion <= TLS 1.1)
attack_scenario: A network MITM strips or blocks TLS 1.2/1.3 in the handshake and forces negotiation down to TLS 1.0/SSLv3, then applies POODLE/BEAST-style block-by-block decryption to recover session cookies or credentials, or exploits RC4 biases to recover repeated plaintext.
negative_test_hint: attempt a handshake offering only "TLS 1.0" and assert the connection is rejected rather than negotiated down to the deprecated protocol

exemplar.explanation: RFC 8996 formally deprecates TLS 1.0/1.1, and BSI TR-02102-2 plus ANSSI 'Recommandations de securite relatives a TLS' require TLS 1.2 as the floor. Setting MinVersion to VersionSSL30/TLS10/TLS11 in a Go tls.Config (or capping MaxVersion there) permits protocol-level weaknesses (BEAST, POODLE, RC4/CBC MAC-then-encrypt) that a peer can be downgraded to, so TLS 1.2 or higher must be the minimum.
